title: Balance sheet, income statement and cash flow
acceptance_authority: Root coordinator only; this is an author audit, not chapter acceptance or external accounting certification.

scope.word_count_method: HTMLParser text nodes and Unicode word regex, excluding HTML tags
scope.assets: Original synthetic 23-event journal, exact integer CU minor-unit stdlib benchmark, JSON inputs and README. All monetary report values are exact decimal strings in kCU.

content_review.prerequisite_and_entity: Read fixed assignment and canonical c01/c02 prerequisites. Coordinated debit-positive ledger, contra asset, normal balances, accrual/closing and owner-transaction interface with c01 author. Harbor Instruments is explicitly a distinct trading corporation with quarter dates and kCU units; not the preceding service-company case.
content_review.statements: Read full chapter and independently reconciled opening 216=110+106, closing 286=143+143, profit25, retained earnings43, contribution20, dividend8 and equity increase37. Book values, market values, liquidation proceeds and payment calendars distinguished. Temporary closures move no cash.
content_review.cash_derivation: Derived each direct operating line from its account roll-forward before summing CFO. Indirect formula explicitly uses normal balances and excludes cash/debt from the stated NWC definition. Conditions excluding writeoffs, acquired balances, FX and cross-account transfers are stated. Interest class changes require removing interest payable and adding the whole expense consistently; Exercise5 gives complete alternate bridge.
content_review.schedules_and_boundaries: Gross/accumulated/net equipment and debt schedules distinguish cash acquisition, disposal cost/book amount/gain, depreciation and noncash seller note18. Current/noncurrent debt21/72 is a supplied schedule, not inferred from names. Loss/zero-gain/positive-gain branches independently checked. No imaginary gross cash flows attributed to the seller note.
content_review.liquidity: Collection20 changes cash to4 and CFO to-44 without changing accrual profit/equity. Collection10 implies unfunded cash-6; explicit negative-prefix validation rejects it, including a case with later funding. Borrow6 or choose dividend2 before declaration gives zero cash with distinct debt/equity claims and no improvement in profit/CFO. No lawful-distribution or future-solvency certification implied.
content_review.recognition_and_control: Balanced wrong-account receipt is a deliberate complete counterexample: profit and AR both overstated5, all numeric bridges still pass. Independent supplied-transaction reference detects it. Loan misclassification can preserve total cash while misallocating CFO/CFF; documentary evidence and correctly scoped indirect bridge are needed.
content_review.solutions: All eight prompts and complete solutions read against each other and recomputed. Exercise1 effects, compact company, reverse working-capital schedules, disposal/noncash note, alternative interest class, financing repairs, cancellation counterexamples and calendar/liquidation comparison verified. Teach-back checklist and delayed collection/reclassification answers supplied.
content_review.sources: Actual accessible primary bodies inspected: 2007 SEC orientation, IAS7 public overview, December2023 SEC staff statement including legal-status footnote, April2024 IFRS18 issuance/effective-date announcement and Effects Analysis p27. Dated scope and standard-versus-teaching convention clear. Full subscription IAS7 body not inspected and not claimed; no source workaround.
content_review.code: Strict bounded schema, exact decimal strings converted to integers, no floats/network/install/randomness, portable default input, 17 explicit residual checks and error paths independent of removable assertions. Report exposes ledger, closures, statements, schedules, cash path and limits. General recognition/measurement questions are intentionally outside the fixed model.

resolved_findings.origin: c01/c02 terminology coordination and author review
resolved_findings.finding: The compact company solution called total assets after accumulated depreciation net assets, which could conflict with net assets meaning equity.
resolved_findings.resolution: Changed to opening total assets70; depreciation effect also uses total assets. Full entity name Harbor Instruments distinguishes the separate c01/c02 companies.
